hero.title: The Kanva Dynasty: Post-Mauryan Transition
hero.description: A brief but significant Brahminical dynasty in Magadha that succeeded the Shungas, marking the waning power of central authority in the Gangetic plains.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The Kanva period covers the transition between the decline of Shunga power and the rise of the Satavahanas.

cards.details: Vasudeva Kanva assassinates the last Shunga ruler, Devabhuti, establishing the Kanva dynasty.
The Kanva rule ends when the Satavahana King Simuka defeats Susarman, the last Kanva king.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Key memory triggers for UPSC Prelims.

items.title: V-B-N-S
items.decryption: These are the four documented kings of the Kanva dynasty in chronological order.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Thinking Kanvas held a vast empire: They were restricted to Magadha and parts of Central India, unlike the Mauryas.
Confusing Kanvas with the Kushanas: Kanvas were indigenous Brahminical rulers, while Kushanas were foreign invaders.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Magadha (Pataliputra)
  • Limited regional influence
  • Struggled against growing Satavahana power

Personalities

  • Vasudeva: Founder (Minister to Devabhuti)
  • Susarman: Last ruler
  • Brahminical lineage emphasized
  • Political Structure
    • Successors of the Shunga dynasty.
    • Rule was essentially a 'shadow of authority' compared to the Mauryas.
    • Brahminical revival continued under their patronage.
  • Decline Factors
    • Lack of military aggression.
    • Internal fragmentation in the Gangetic Valley.
    • Rise of regional powers like the Satavahanas in the Deccan and Chetis in Kalinga.
